After over a decade of not using touch screens in its Mac laptop lineup, Apple is finally set to launch its first MacBook with a touch screen as early as October. The new machine will be released alongside the next-generation MacBook Pro redesign, tentatively named the MacBook Ultra.

Of course, rumours remain rumours — but almost all reliable sources believe the MacBook Pro will gain touch support later this year. Apple has even dropped hints in macOS 27: Sidecar touch support, pull-to-refresh, and slightly enlarged menu bar items.

As a 13-inch MacBook Air user, this is particularly annoying, because content that previously fit just to the left of the notch now gets pushed below.

You can chalk it all up to coincidence, but the reality is probably exactly what it appears to be on the surface. Either way, here's what the first MacBook with a touch screen will bring.

OLED, Dynamic Island

On the display front, the redesigned MacBook Pro will feature a Tandem OLED display, similar to the technology used in the iPad Pro, which is widely regarded as one of the best portable displays on the market. Tandem OLED consists of multiple stacked layers of OLED panels, delivering outstanding colour performance, extremely high contrast, and greater brightness.

There are also reports that the new machine will feature a Dynamic Island, albeit slightly smaller than the one on the iPhone. However, it will not support Face ID.

Software optimisation

According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple will make several special optimisations for the first MacBook Pro with a touch screen, going beyond what is currently visible in the macOS 27 beta:

"For example, when users touch a button or control, a new menu will pop up near the user's finger, offering options better suited to touch operation. The software will also display the most appropriate set of controls based on the user's past operation history. Additionally, if users tap menu bar items at the top of the screen, that set of controls will enlarge for easier finger selection."

M5 Pro and M5 Max chips

Although earlier reports suggested the redesigned MacBook Pro would debut M6 Pro and M6 Max chips, Apple has now decided to skip these chips to accelerate the development of the M7. This means the first batch of 2nm chips will not be used in this redesigned MacBook Pro; the new machine will continue to use the existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.

However, a base model version will not be available for now. There are rumours that Apple will launch a redesigned MacBook Pro base model with an M7 chip as early as next spring.

Slightly thinner body

As for the design of the new MacBook Pro, one rumour suggests the new machine will be slightly thinner and lighter — but exactly how noticeable the difference will be remains unknown. The previous-generation MacBook Pro has a fairly chunky appearance and feel, so any improvement in this area would be welcome — provided thermal performance is not compromised as a result.

Summary

Overall, the first MacBook Pro with a touch screen will be an exciting upgrade. With Apple having raised prices in June due to tight memory supply, the new machine's pricing will be higher — the 14-inch model is expected to start from US$2,499 at minimum, while the 16-inch model starts from US$2,999.

Are you excited about a MacBook with a touch screen? Will you pick one up as soon as it launches, or will you wait for a more affordable 14-inch base model? Let us know in the comments.
